title: Shift descent and finite-model reflection of common-stage distinguished triangles
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible, in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]; such schemes are called allowed. For each finite $E\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, use the framework integral category and raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E^s(T)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and the PBC integral category and raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E^p(T)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category].
Use these categories also for each allowed $W$, with $T$ replaced by $W$. For each allowed scheme $W$ and every finite $E$, suppose given exact $E$-linear equivalences $J_{W,E}:\mathcal C_E^s(W)\simeq\mathcal C_E^p(W)$ and exact natural scalar comparisons $j_{W,L/E}:J_{W,L}S_{L/E}\simeq P_{L/E}J_{W,E}$. Here $S,P$ and their associators $a^s,a^p$ are the actual transitions of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition, prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Assume the identity normalization, compatibility with shifts and the scalar cocycle
$$a^p_{M,L,E}\circ P_{M/L}(j_{W,L/E})\circ j_{W,M/L,S_{L/E}K}=j_{W,M/E}\circ J_{W,M}(a^s_{M,L,E}).$$
Write $\mathcal C_W,\mathcal P_W$ for the literal pair categories of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], with inclusions $\iota^s_E,\iota^p_E$. All categories are viewed in one sufficiently large universe. Let $J_W:\mathcal C_W\to\mathcal P_W$ be the additive functor sending $(E,K)$ to $(E,J_{W,E}K)$ and, for $u:S_{M/E}K\to S_{M/F}H$, with
$$J_W[M,u]=[M,j_{W,M/F,H}J_{W,M}(u)j_{W,M/E,K}^{-1}],$$
and assume its induced Hom maps are bijective. For the specified finite exact-functor comparisons $\delta_{W,E}:J_{W,E}(-[1])\simeq(J_{W,E}-)[1]$, the classes $[E,\delta_{W,E,K}]$ form a natural shift isomorphism $J_W(-[1])\simeq(J_W-)[1]$ for the actual pair shifts, with inverse classes $[E,\delta_{W,E,K}^{-1}]$. Under $J_W\iota^s_E=\iota^p_EJ_{W,E}$ this is the prescribed finite-stage comparison; the corresponding integer-shift comparisons have the same property. The image of every distinguished triangle of $\mathcal C_W$ is distinguished in $\mathcal P_W$. Conversely, for every triangle $D$ of $\mathcal C_W$ whose image is distinguished, there exist a finite $M$, a distinguished triangle $A$ in $\mathcal C^p_M(W)$, and an exact quasi-inverse $R_M$ of $J_{W,M}$ such that
$$J_WD\simeq\iota^p_M A,\qquad D\simeq\iota^s_M R_M A.$$
Every common-stage cone of $[M,u]:(E,K)\to(F,H)$ identifies with the inclusion of its stage-$M$ cone by the endpoint classes $[M,\operatorname{id}]$, with third arrow $[M,(\sigma^p_{M/E,K})^{-1}p_u]$ as in [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. The image under $J_W$ of the second triangle isomorphism is the composite of the finite exact-equivalence isomorphism $J_{W,M}R_M A\simeq A$ with the first triangle isomorphism, using the descended shift comparison. Hence $J_W$ preserves and reflects distinguished triangles. Every quasi-inverse, with the shift comparison induced from the equivalence, is exact as well. These assertions concern the raw pair categories, without Karoubi completion.

proof.text: Use the generic pairCommShift construction from SfFrameworkCommonStageDescent, specialized to the framework source and actual PBC target. Its finite-stage formula is the inverse source inclusion shift, the included finite comparison and the target inclusion shift. The framework inclusion comparison is eqToHom and the PBC inclusion comparison is the identity; removing these transports gives exactly both required HEq formulas. Functor extensionality and functor_map_ι give the literal finite-restriction equality.

For a source distinguished triangle choose its included finite distinguished model using GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.distinguished_iff. The descended inclusion comparison commutes with shifts by pairRestrictionShift. Finite exactness and exactness of the PBC stage inclusion identify its mapped triangle with a distinguished triangle. Transport back along mapTriangleCompIso and the image of the finite-model isomorphism.

The assumed Hom bijections supply Full and Faithful for J.functor. Mathlib Functor.map_distinguished_iff then gives preservation and reflection. The Full and Faithful instances for mapTriangle lift triangle isomorphisms, including their third square, using the descended shift comparison.

For a distinguished image, the common-stage distinguished-set criterion gives M, A and alpha. Take the inverse R=(J.Φ M).inv and the adjunction from (J.Φ M).asEquivalence. Give R adj.rightAdjointCommShift; Adjunction.commShift_of_leftAdjoint and Adjunction.isTriangulated_rightAdjoint give shift compatibility and finite inverse exactness. Build c:J_M(R A)≅A from mapTriangleCompIso, mapTriangleIso of the counit and mapTriangleIdIso. Compose the descended inclusion comparison and its triangle composition isomorphisms with the inclusion of c to obtain e. A generic private stage-system calculation gives its components as the included components of c, hence exactly as the included finite counit components.

Set beta=J.functor.mapTriangle.preimageIso(alpha ≪≫ e.symm). Map-preimage and cancellation of e.inv≫e.hom prove J(beta.hom)≫e.hom=alpha.hom. For any supplied global right adjoint with compatible shift, Adjunction.isTriangulated_rightAdjoint applies directly to the established exact J.functor, proving the final inverse exactness clause.

Retain the already proved fdCommonStageConeIdentification: use isoToStage at the endpoints and identity at the third object. The normalized right-unit associators give the endpoint representative formulas; transition shift compatibility cancels the inverse scalar shift in the connecting arrow.
